generated_test_cases.title: Verify get_db returns a database session
generated_test_cases.description: Ensure that calling get_db returns a valid SQLAlchemy session instance that can be used to query the database.
steps: Call the get_db function without any parameters.
Assert that the returned object is an instance of SQLAlchemy Session.
expected_results: get_db returns a non-null Session object.
Session is usable for simple queries.

generated_test_cases.title: Handle missing database URL environment variable
generated_test_cases.description: Test behavior when the DATABASE_URL environment variable is not set, ensuring an appropriate exception is raised.
steps: Unset or omit the DATABASE_URL environment variable.
expected_results: get_db raises a RuntimeError or a custom configuration exception.

generated_test_cases.title: Boundary: Session lifecycle and cleanup
generated_test_cases.description: Verify that the database session returned by get_db is properly closed after use, preventing resource leaks.
steps: Call get_db to obtain a session.
Use the session to perform a query.
Ensure the session is closed or disposed after use, e.g., via context manager or explicit close.
expected_results: Session is closed after the test completes.
No open connections remain.

generated_test_cases.title: Security: Prevent SQL injection via session creation
generated_test_cases.description: Ensure that get_db does not incorporate user input into raw SQL statements during session creation, mitigating injection risks.
steps: Mock or inject a malicious DATABASE_URL containing SQL payload.
Call get_db and attempt to perform a harmless operation.
Verify that the session is created using parameterized URLs and no execution of injected SQL occurs.
expected_results: No SQL injection occurs; the session is safe to use.

generated_test_cases.title: Exception handling: Database connection failure
generated_test_cases.description: Test get_db behavior when the database server is unreachable, ensuring graceful exception handling.
steps: Configure DATABASE_URL to point to an unavailable host or port.
Catch the resulting OperationalError or connection exception.
expected_results: get_db raises an OperationalError or custom database connection exception.
Error message is informative and does not leak sensitive details.

expected_results: HTTP 404 Not Found returned

generated_test_cases.title: Uppercase discount code - positive
generated_test_cases.description: Verify that the uppercase_discount method correctly converts a lowercase discount code to uppercase.
steps: Create a Checkout instance with discount_code set to "save10".
expected_results: The discount_code attribute is transformed to "SAVE10".

generated_test_cases.title: Uppercase discount code - negative null input
generated_test_cases.description: Check behavior when discount_code is None; method should handle gracefully without raising an exception.
steps: Create a Checkout instance with discount_code set to null.
expected_results: The method leaves discount_code as None and does not raise an error.

generated_test_cases.title: Uppercase discount code - boundary empty string
generated_test_cases.description: Validate that an empty string discount_code remains unchanged after calling uppercase_discount.
steps: Create a Checkout instance with discount_code set to an empty string "".
expected_results: The discount_code remains an empty string.

generated_test_cases.title: Uppercase discount code - security injection attempt
generated_test_cases.description: Ensure that passing a malicious string does not execute code or alter system state.
steps: Create a Checkout instance with discount_code set to "<script>alert(1)</script>".
expected_results: The discount_code is transformed to "<SCRIPT>ALERT(1)</SCRIPT>" without executing any script.

generated_test_cases.title: Uppercase discount code - exception handling during integration
generated_test_cases.description: Simulate a failure in the underlying model serialization to verify that uppercase_discount propagates exceptions appropriately.
steps: Mock the Checkout model's __dict__ method to raise a RuntimeError when accessed.
Create a Checkout instance and call uppercase_discount.
expected_results: A RuntimeError is raised and caught by the calling code, indicating proper exception propagation.
